newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia law chief re-opens probe of top minister.
newsitem.headline: Colombia law chief re-opens probe of top minister.

text.p: Colombia's chief prosecutor re-opened an investigation on Friday into Interior Minister Horacio Serpa's role in the alleged use of drug money to finance President Ernesto Samper's 1994 re-election campaign.

Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso, a fervent anti-drug crusader, said the probes of former Foreign Relations Minister Rodrigo Pardo and ex-Communications Minister Juan Manuel Turbay, for the same alleged offences, would also be re-opened.
Serpa, one of the embattled president's closest allies, told reporters he would cooperate with the official inquiry but would not step down from his post until it concluded.

The investigation of Serpa, Pardo and Turbay was shelved in July because of a legal technicality. At the same time, a congressional inquiry cleared Samper of any blame connected to allegations that he received millions of dollars in Cali drug cartel cash to fund his presidential campaign.
